implementing Regulation (EU) 2020/1998 concerning restrictive measures against s, para 8

paras.text: On 8 December 2020, by way of the Declaration by the High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy (the ‘High Representative’), on behalf of the European Union, regarding the EU Global Human Rights Sanctions Regime, the Union and its Member States reaffirmed their strong commitment to the promotion and protection of human rights around the world. The EU Global Human Rights Sanctions Regime underscores the Union’s determination to enhance its role in addressing serious human rights violations and abuses worldwide. Achieving the effective enjoyment of human rights by everyone is a strategic goal of the Union. Respect for human dignity, freedom, democracy, equality, the rule of law and human rights is a fundamental value of the Union and its common foreign and security policy.
paras.loc: implementing Regulation (EU) 2020/1998 concerning restrictive measures against s, para 9
implementing Regulation (EU) 2020/1998 concerning restrictive measures against s, para 10

paras.text: In its statement before the United Nations Security Council on 24 June 2026, the Union expressed grave concern at the unprecedented increase in grave violations against children in armed conflict, stressed the importance of preventing such violations and ensuring accountability for those responsible, and called on all parties to armed conflict to uphold their obligations under international law and take concrete steps to end and prevent violations against children.
paras.loc: implementing Regulation (EU) 2020/1998 concerning restrictive measures against s, para 11
implementing Regulation (EU) 2020/1998 concerning restrictive measures against s, para 12

paras.text: In that context, four entities should be added to the list of natural or legal persons, entities or bodies subject to restrictive measures in Annex I to Regulation (EU) 2020/1998.
paras.loc: implementing Regulation (EU) 2020/1998 concerning restrictive measures against s, para 13
implementing Regulation (EU) 2020/1998 concerning restrictive measures against s, para 14

paras.text: Regulation (EU) 2020/1998 should therefore be amended accordingly,
paras.loc: implementing Regulation (EU) 2020/1998 concerning restrictive measures against s, para 15

paras.text: HAS ADOPTED THIS REGULATION:
paras.loc: implementing Regulation (EU) 2020/1998 concerning restrictive measures against s, para 16

paras.text: Annex I to Regulation (EU) 2020/1998 is amended in accordance with the Annex to this Regulation.
This Regulation shall enter into force on the date of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union .
This Regulation shall be binding in its entirety and directly applicable in all Member States.
Done at Brussels, 16 November 2026.
For the Council
The President
K. KALLAS

5 Segond
Address: Village de Dieu, Port-au-Prince, Haiti Type of entity: non-State armed criminal gang

5 Segond is a criminal armed group operating in Haiti. 5 Segond is responsible for killings, rape and other forms of sexual and gender-based violence, kidnapping, extortion, theft, piracy, obstruction of humanitarian aid, attacks against civilians and civilian infrastructure, and arms and drug trafficking. 5 Segond has committed grave violations against children, including sexual violence. Members of 5 Segond were identified as responsible for the rape of two girls, aged 3 and 12, at a site for internally displaced persons in March 2024. The group has also carried out attacks affecting health infrastructure and humanitarian services. 5 Segond is therefore responsible for serious human rights violations and abuses, including systematic and widespread sexual and gender-based violence.
400 Mawozo
Address: Croix-des-Bouquets, Port-au-Prince metropolitan area, Haiti Type of entity: non-State armed criminal gang

400 Mawozo is a criminal armed group operating in Haiti. 400 Mawozo is responsible for the recruitment and exploitation of children, exposing them to armed violence and other serious abuses. 400 Mawozo is further responsible for killings, rape and other forms of sexual and gender-based violence, including rape of minors, kidnapping, attacks against civilians, looting, destruction of public property, hijacking of trucks, attacks disrupting humanitarian assistance, and forced displacement. 400 Mawozo is therefore responsible for serious human rights violations and abuses, killings, and systematic and widespread sexual and gender-based violence.
Gran Ravine
Address: Port-au-Prince ouest, Haiti Type of entity: non-State armed criminal gang

Gran Ravine is a criminal armed group operating in Haiti. Gran Ravine is responsible for killings, rape and other forms of sexual and gender-based violence, kidnapping, attacks against civilians, destruction of property, and other acts of violence against civilian populations. Under the leadership of Renel Destina, alias “Ti Lapli”, Gran Ravine has committed murder, rape, kidnapping, and other serious crimes. The group has carried out attacks resulting in civilian deaths, displacement, and the disruption of essential services. Gran Ravine is therefore responsible for serious human rights violations and abuses, including killings and systematic and widespread sexual and gender-based violence.
Krazé Baryè
Address: Port-au-Prince metropolitan area, including Pétion-Ville and surrounding communes Type of entity: non-State armed criminal gang

Krazé Baryè is a criminal armed group operating primarily in the Port-au-Prince metropolitan area of Haiti. Krazé Baryè is responsible for the recruitment and exploitation of children, exposing them to armed violence and other serious abuses. Krazé Baryè is further responsible for killings, rape and other forms of sexual and gender-based violence, kidnapping, attacks against civilians, destruction of property, and forced displacement. Krazé Baryè is therefore responsible for serious human rights violations and abuses, including the recruitment and exploitation of children, the killing and maiming of children, killings, and systematic and widespread sexual and gender-based violence.
